taxonomic_note: Accepted distinct Funastrum crispum (Kew POWO and Flora of North America). Historical Sarcostemma and Philibertia concepts may persist on source specimen labels. Be cautious with names heterophyllum: Funastrum heterophyllum is a different accepted taxon and is NOT automatically a synonym of F. crispum in current Kew treatment.
look_here_first: FLATTEN A MATURE LEAF in view: leaf edge often WAVY/crisped and blade narrow TRIANGULAR, with heart-shaped base. Then inspect an OPEN FLOWER face: large (~20 mm across), brownish/orange to green, 5 broad spreading lobes; white-pink fleshy corona inside. Unlike climbing milkweed F. cynanchoides, flowers generally are larger and lack the many cream/rose-tinged little petals. Confirm flowers and fruit when leaf margins are not obviously curled.

project_inclusion.range_basis: POWO/FNA confirm Texas native and UT Austin Williamson County flora documents the taxon in Williamson; Hays and additional project counties not independently certified in this pass.

morphology_keys.life_cycle: Perennial herbaceous, twining and trailing milkvine; multiple long slender stems and white milky latex.
morphology_keys.stems: Cylindrical twining stems up to ~2 mm diameter; short DOWNWARD-CURVED simple hairs (0.1–0.2 mm) plus inconspicuous glandular hairs; no tendrils.
morphology_keys.leaves: Opposite, decussate, simple, short-petiolate, typically triangular to narrowly triangular blades (about 25–75 mm long), cordate at base; often wavy/crispate edges but sometimes almost flat. Many upper sun leaves are narrower; leaf pairs may be unequal in size.
morphology_keys.inflorescence: Axillary umbel-like cymes, often roughly hemispheric clusters of up to ~9 comparatively large flowers on a short hairy peduncle.
morphology_keys.flowers: Corolla five-lobed, rotate, roughly 20 mm across, lobes about 10 mm long; upper-facing petals orange to brown or greenish, short-ciliate along margins; typically glabrous inside. Corolla color changes with age, so use leaf edge and larger flowers together.
morphology_keys.corona: Five fleshy thumb-like segments, often pink/rose and white, visibly constricted around midlength (Flora of North America key). These are NOT separate petals; inspect central milkweed gynostegium and pollinia.
morphology_keys.fruits: One or two long slender follicles, often ~10–13 cm; seeds furnished with silky white hairs (coma). Pods can be more diagnostic than flower color when mature.
best_field_traits: larger brown/orange-green starry corollas ~20 mm diameter
flower crown of pink-white thick coronas with median waist
short-haired axillary cymes, white milky latex
field_id_sequence: Check a mature leaf for a wavy crispate margin; consider flat variation.
Follow the opposite leaf pair to an axillary flower cluster; no twining tendrils.
Look directly at flower size and five broad warm-toned petals; center has five thick pink/white coronas.
Check fine curved stem hairs and flower inside with 10x loupe.
Use long pods and mature fruit measurements if flowers ambiguous.
cautions: Wavy leaf margins can be subtle or absent on some shoots; do not ID from leaf edge alone.
Older taxonomy or common name 'climbing milkweed' is shared; scientific name/source concept must be checked.
Funastrum heterophyllum and trans-Pecos varieties often historically filed under Sarcostemma cynanchoides; do not substitute photos.

confused_with: Funastrum heterophyllum (different accepted name, external look-alike)
comparisons.key_distinctions: Against F. cynanchoides, crispum typically has more markedly crisped/undulate leaf edges, bigger orange/brown/green ~20mm corollas with glabrous inner surface and a constricted five-part corona, versus flatter-edged leaves, smaller creamy/rose flowers and inflated glossy white corona tips. Talayote/Cynanchum unifarium has much smaller ~5mm flowers in branched raceme-like axillary spray; Matelea reticulata has dark-reticulate broad flattened green star with brilliant silver pearl center.
